review_notes: Read the whole target file, the Mathlib WithVal/WithAbs simp API (toVal_ofVal and toAbs_ofAbs are simp; ofVal_toVal and ofAbs_toAbs are not), and the downstream tests in ValuationIntegersTest/AbsoluteValue.lean. There is no loop or competing-rule problem: the two @[simp] apply lemmas have distinct left-hand sides. The `_toEquiv` lemma is correctly not simp. The one concern is incomplete simp coverage of the common composites. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether simp currently closes these goals through other rules. The finding is moderate confidence and based only on how the tests are written.

findings.excerpt: v.absoluteValueUniformEquiv x = WithAbs.toAbs v.absoluteValue x.ofVal := rfl
findings.problem: The simp interface stops at `toAbs _ x.ofVal` and `toVal v x.ofAbs`. The usual way to use the equivalence is on `WithVal.toVal v q` for `q : K`, or to read off `.ofAbs` of the result. In Mathlib the cancellation lemmas `WithVal.ofVal_toVal` and `WithAbs.ofAbs_toAbs` are not simp (only `toVal_ofVal` and `toAbs_ofAbs` are). So after the apply lemma fires, the normal form is `toAbs _ (toVal v q).ofVal`, or `(toAbs _ x.ofVal).ofAbs`. Neither reduces to the underlying element by simp. The downstream tests do not rely on simp for this: they restate the fact as a hand-written `hmap` and prove it by `absoluteValueUniformEquiv_apply _ _`. The target's own proofs also pass `WithAbs.ofAbs_toAbs` explicitly to `simpa only`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` lemmas for the composites that stay in the intended normal form (the underlying element wrapped once). The suggested statements are `v.absoluteValueUniformEquiv (WithVal.toVal v x) = WithAbs.toAbs v.absoluteValue x`, `(v.absoluteValueUniformEquiv x).ofAbs = x.ofVal`, `v.absoluteValueUniformEquiv.symm (WithAbs.toAbs v.absoluteValue x) = WithVal.toVal v x` and `(v.absoluteValueUniformEquiv.symm x).ofVal = x.ofAbs`. All should be provable by `rfl`. Alternatively, state the existing `_apply` lemmas on the composed forms and keep the general ones too. Tests can then use `simp` instead of a local `hmap`.
findings.benefit: Users who compute with the uniform equivalence on `toVal` and `toAbs` elements get the underlying-element normal form from `simp` in one step. They no longer need a local `hmap` or a manual `ofAbs_toAbs` rewrite. The new lemmas are rfl-lemmas that strictly reduce the term, so they add no loop risk.

evidence.excerpt: lemma ofAbs_toAbs (x : R) : ofAbs (toAbs v x) = x := rfl
lemma ofVal_toVal (x : R) : ofVal (toVal v x) = x := rfl
